append.text: **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:9 in DO's ids) *dedúcit ad ínferos et redúcit* → *faz descer aos infernos e traz de volta*** (v2). The noun and *traz de volta* are 212's; **the verb is not.** The v1 Latinist found *conduz* (212's *conduzis*) loses the downward motion of *de-dúcere* that pairs with *re-dúcere*, and the *dedúcere* row (D22, with D25's note: 7:6, 21:16, 54:24) already gives *fazer descer* for a descent. The CNBB LH and Lectionary also say *faz descer* here. **So the ruling on this row should cover the verb too: 212 *conduzis … e trazeis de volta* against 223 *faz descer … e traz de volta*; if *fazer descer* stands, 212 becomes *fazeis descer aos infernos, e trazeis de volta*.** The 223 ambiguity reader again heard the hell of the damned. Options in ps223 `deducit` (*conduz* = 212; the stylist's *conduz … e reconduz*, refused because *reconduzir* is heard of officials) and `inferos` (*à morada dos mortos*, *ao inferno*). Passed the v2 gate.
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:9) *dedúcit ad ínferos* → *faz descer aos infernos*** — see the formula row *ad ínferos* (for Gustavo).

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:1, 2:16) *exaltátum est cornu meum* → *foi exaltado o meu chifre*; *sublimábit cornu Christi sui* → *alçará o chifre do seu Cristo*** — the canticle's inclusio kept with one noun; the order of 88:25 (the stylist's subject-first order refused on that precedent). The ambiguity reader heard a literal horn and did not know the metaphor. *força* (MS1932) and *fronte* (the CNBB's paraphrase) are options.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:2) *Dilatátum est os meum super inimícos meos* → *Dilatou-se a minha boca sobre os meus inimigos*** (v2, then the gate). v1 had 80:11's idiom (*Abriu-se bem*); the Latinist and the stylist both asked the cognate (MS1932), and the ambiguity reader heard *bem* as 'rightly'. *super* → *sobre* at the gate (triumph over, not 34:21's *contra*; 21:14 *Abriram sobre mim a sua boca*). A fourth place for the cognate, with 118:32.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:9) *dedúcit ad ínferos* → *faz descer aos infernos*** (v2, the Latinist; the *fazer descer* of 7:6, 21:16, 54:24). Canticle 212's *conduzis aos infernos* did not meet this row; see *ad ínferos*.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:5) *Deus scientiárum* → *o Deus dos saberes*** (the row's noun in the Latin's plural; the Hebrew's is plural too). The stylist heard *saberes* as academic and asked *conhecimentos* (refused: a new word for the row); the ambiguity reader found the plural 'somewhat odd'. *o Deus do saber*, *de todo o saber* (DRB) options.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:12) *sólium glóriæ téneat* → *ocupe um trono de glória*** — a local departure (MS1932): *tome um trono* is heard as usurping. The stylist heard *ocupe* as administrative and asked *tenha* (refused, weak); both options.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:9) *Dóminus mortíficat et vivíficat* → *O Senhor dá a morte e dá a vida*** — the row's option used locally, to keep the Latin's twin verbs (*mortificáre → dar a morte*, 36:32); the Brazilian Lectionary's line. No reader remarked. *dá a morte e vivifica* option.
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:9) *mortíficat* → *dá a morte*** (paired with *dá a vida*).

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:16) *cornu Christi sui* → *o chifre do seu Cristo*** (D19; MS1932 the same). The ambiguity reader heard Jesus Christ; the CNBB LH, Lectionary, DM1962 and DO's Portuguese say *Ungido* (option).
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:16) *dabit impérium regi suo* → *dará o domínio ao seu rei*** — one of the canticle places this row named; no reader remarked.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:6) *Arcus fórtium superátus est* → *O arco dos fortes foi vencido*** — a local departure: of a beaten bow *foi superado* is heard as 'surpassed'. DRB 'overcome'. *superado* option. No reader remarked.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:11) *Súscitat de púlvere egénum* → *Levanta do pó o necessitado*** (112:7's build), kept apart from *exaltar*, *erguer* (subleváre), *elevar* and *alçar* (sublimáre) in the same canticle.
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:11) *de stércore élevat páuperem* → *e do esterco eleva o pobre*** (*eleváre → elevar*; 112:7 has *érigens → ergue*).
Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:11) *egénum … páuperem* → *o necessitado … o pobre* (D38).
Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:13) *pósuit super eos orbem* → *sobre eles pôs o mundo* (D30).
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:7) *pro pánibus se locavérunt* → *se empregaram por pão*** (D42). The Latinist asked *pães* at v1 and again at the gate (minor); refused both times on D42.
**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:15) *Dóminum formidábunt adversárii ejus* → *Do Senhor terão pavor os seus adversários*** (the Latin's fronted object kept first).
Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:8) *stérilis péperit plúrimos* → *a estéril deu à luz a muitos*.
Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:14) *conticéscent* → *se calarão* — see the new row *conticéscere*.

**Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:14) *non in fortitúdine sua roborábitur vir* → *porque o homem não se fortalecerá pela sua força*** (*roboráre* → *fortalecer-se*; v2 the stylist's plain order for v1's cleft *não é … que*).
Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:12) *sólium glóriæ* → *um trono de glória* (sólium, a king's seat, shares *trono*).

terms: | cardo (*cárdines terræ*) | eixo (*Porque do Senhor são os eixos da terra*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:13)**; not a psalter word (concord). *cardo*: a door's hinge, then the pivot on which the sky turns (L&S). v1 had *os polos* (DRB, MS1932); the stylist and the ambiguity reader both heard the North and South Poles, and the stylist asked *eixos*. *polos*, *gonzos* options; the CNBB and DM1962 have *colunas* (the Hebrew-family text). |

| róbur | vigor (*e os fracos foram cingidos de vigor*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:6)**; not a psalter word. Keeps *força* for fortitúdo (2:14 in the same canticle) and *poder* for virtus; the CNBB's word in the same line. *robustez* option. |

| se locáre (*pro pánibus se locavérunt*) | empregar-se (*se empregaram por pão*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:7)**; 'hire oneself out' (DRB). The stylist heard a modern job search and asked *alugaram-se* (option 2: heard of renting property in Brazil); the ambiguity reader heard 'hired themselves out for bread' as meant. MS1932 *se assalariaram* option. |

| conticéscere | calar-se (*e os ímpios se calarão nas trevas*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:14)**; inchoative of *tacére*, whose row it shares; kept apart from *obmutéscere → emudecer* (D39). *emudecerão* option. |

| vétera (neuter plural) | as coisas velhas (*Afastem-se da vossa boca as coisas velhas*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:5)**; *velho* for *vetus*, keeping *antigo* for *antíquus* (43:2b, 76:6, 142:5). The ambiguity reader found it vague, as the Latin is. *as coisas antigas*, MS1932 *a antiga linguagem* options. |

| sublimáre | alçar (*e alçará o chifre do seu Cristo*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:16)**; not a psalter word. Kept apart from *exaltar* (2:1, the same canticle's inclusio), *elevar* (eleváre), *erguer* (subleváre here) and *levantar* (suscitáre). The ambiguity reader did not know *alçará*; kept. *exaltará* (MS1932, CNBB) merges with 2:1. |

| subleváre | erguer (*humilha e ergue*) | open | **Canticle 223 (1 Sam 2:10)**; not a psalter word. *erguer* is also *extóllere*'s and *attóllere*'s (133:2, 23:7) and 112:7's *érigens*; none of them meets it here. MS1932 and the CNBB *exalta* would merge with 2:1. *soergue* option. |
